title: An electrostatic repulsion model of centromere organisation.
authors: Bell, Caelan; Chen, Lifeng; Maristany, M Julia; Blaukopf, Claudia; Zhou, Huabin; Huertas, Jan; Perez Lopez, Jose I; Langer, Christoph C H; Steinacker, Thomas L; Schutte, Nikki; Doolittle, Lynda K; Espinosa, Jorge R; Redding, Sy; Collepardo-Guevara, Rosana; Rosen, Michael K; Gerlich, Daniel W
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
one_liner_zh: 该文通过多尺度分子动力学模拟和生化重构，揭示着丝粒蛋白CENP-B的静电排斥驱动着丝粒在染色质表面定位，并涉及相分离机制，虽对象非典型IDP但互作机制建模与相分离背景对本课题有启发。
abstract: During cell division, chromosomes reorganise into compact bodies in which centromeres localise precisely at the chromatin surface(1-4) to enable kinetochore-microtubule interactions essential for genome segregation(5-8). The physical principles guiding this centromere positioning remain unknown. Here, we reveal that human core centromeres are directed to the chromatin surface by repulsion of centromere-associated proteins - independent of condensin-mediated loop extrusion and microtubule engagement. Using cellular perturbations, biochemical reconstitution, and multiscale molecular dynamics simulations, we show that chromatin surface localisation emerges from repulsion between condensed chromatin and both the kinetochore and the highly negatively charged centromere protein, CENP-B. Together, these elements form a centromeric region composed of two domains with opposing affinities, one favouring integration within the mitotic chromosome and the other favouring exposure to the surrounding cytoplasm, thereby driving surface positioning. Tethering synthetic negatively charged proteins to chromatin was sufficient to recapitulate this surface localisation in cells and in vitro, indicating that electrostatic repulsion is a key determinant of surface localisation. These findings demonstrate that centromere layering is not hardwired by chromatin folding patterns but instead emerges from phase separation in chromatin. Our work uncovers electrostatic polarity as a general and programmable mechanism to spatially organise chromatin.
abstract_zh: 在细胞分裂过程中，染色体重组为紧凑结构，其中着丝粒精确定位于染色质表面(1-4)，以促进着丝粒-微管相互作用，这对基因组分离至关重要(5-8)。引导这种着丝粒定位的物理原理仍属未知。在此，我们揭示人类核心着丝粒通过着丝粒相关蛋白的排斥作用被导向染色质表面——这一过程独立于凝缩蛋白介导的环挤压和微管结合。利用细胞扰动、生化重构及多尺度分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟，我们表明染色质表面定位源于浓缩染色质与着丝粒及高度带负电荷的着丝粒蛋白CENP-B之间的排斥作用。这些元素共同形成一个由两个具有相反亲和力结构域组成的着丝粒区域，一个有利于整合入有丝分裂染色体，另一个则有利于暴露于周围细胞质，从而驱动表面定位。将合成的带负电荷蛋白拴系至染色质，足以在细胞和体外重现这种表面定位，表明静电排斥是表面定位的关键决定因素。这些发现证明着丝粒分层并非由染色质折叠模式硬性编码，而是源于染色质中的相分离 (phase separation)。我们的工作揭示了静电极性作为一种通用且可编程的机制，用于空间组织染色质。
